sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r5/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 12 (#11 timeouts_fit_the_work) and Internal Quality Checks row 12 ('inner < outer, sum of judges < verifier')
evidence: Nesting arithmetic holds on the frozen bytes. task.toml: [agent].timeout_sec=7200, build_timeout_sec=600, [verifier].timeout_sec=13200 (identical to the template and staged-task-contract.md 53-75). test.sh (byte-identical to template) runs rewardkit with --max-concurrent-agent 1 (line 207), gates budget 1500 (line 213), scored budget 11100 (line 224). Gates: render 600 + constraints 600 = 1200 < 1500 (each also < 1500). Scored: functional mode=individual, timeout=550 per criterion x 16 criteria (counted 16 [[criterion]] blocks) = 8800, + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10600 < 11100 (each judge < 11100). Budgets: 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200, leaving 600 s for copy/startup/liveness (120 x 0.25 s ready loop, ~30 s nominal) and score.py; 13200 < 18000 five-hour limit. Liveness: test.sh 30 s ready loop; restart helper 5 s kill wait + 30 s ready loop fits restart_mcp's 55 s cap. Only deviation from template is functional batched/9000 -> individual/550, recorded with reason and authorization in functional/judge.toml lines 7-11 (lead instruction relayed 8 Oct 2026), with the line-9 arithmetic matching mine; it does not increase any budget. Per-criterion semantics are corroborated by the hosted v2 Oracle run (same 550 cap): verifier wall 05:21:17-06:24:16 (~3780 s) with all 16 functional criteria graded 1.0, which is impossible under a single 550 s dimension cap since functional must have taken >= 3780-1200-1800 = 780 s. v2 verifier walls (~63 min Oracle, ~76 min GPT-5.6) are far below 13200; agent run took ~8 min of 7200; cold build is two apt/npm layers, plausible within 600. RISK: the indexed scope states v3 adds legs to five functional criteria and v3 judge durations are unmeasured; no per-criterion duration exists even for v2, and the judge.toml comment itself says 'Not yet measured against a judge run'. Per REVIEW_POLICY line 25 that measurement cannot be waived.
counterexample: Conforming-alternative risk (not a confirmed defect): a correct but slower app (e.g. multi-second transcript or search responses) combined with a v3 functional criterion that now carries extra legs plus a process restart could push a single individual judge session past 550 s, so a correct criterion is cut off and scored as a failure, even though the scored suite as a whole has headroom. No measured run on v3 bytes rules this out.
suggested_fix: No config change required for this row. Obtain a full configured judge run on the v3 bytes and record per-criterion functional durations (max vs 550 s) and gates/scored suite wall times; only if a criterion is measured near the cap, raise its timeout with recorded reason/authorization while keeping 16 x t + 1800 < 11100.
